newsitem.title: USA: La. Republican mulls challenge to primary voting.
newsitem.headline: La. Republican mulls challenge to primary voting.

text.p: A Louisiana Republican who lost a primary runoff election in the state's 7th Congressional District by eight votes is mulling a lawsuit challenging the results, his attorney said Thursday.

Democrats stand to pick up their first Republican seat in Congress unless David Thibodaux can persuade a court to overturn the primary results, which put two Democrats on the November ballot for the district's House seat.

"If we do not file a suit challenging the election the results will become definitive and unassailable," said New Orleans attorney Ben Bagert, who represents Thibodaux and is investigating allegations of impropriety in primary voting.

Bagert said there were reports of seals removed or broken on four voting machines in St. Landry Parish, while other parishes reported more votes cast than the number of voters who actually made it to the polls Saturday.

"We are not saying that happened. People are telling us that happened," he said. "If we can validate (the allegations), then we will bring the suit." Thibodaux has until Monday to challenge the vote count.

According to election results certified Wednesday by the Louisiana secretary of state, Republican Thibodaux, a Lafayette college professor, had 38,590 votes to 38,598 for Democrat Hunter Lundy, a Lake Charles lawyer. The front-runner was Chris John of Crowley.

Wade Martin, chief elections officer for the Louisiana secretary of state, told reporters the election was the closest in state history. The primary was an open election, in which members of all parties competed.

The southwest Louisiana seat became vacant when Jimmy Haines, a Lafayette Republican, sought election to the U.S. Senate. If the results stand, Democrats would pick up the first of 19 Republican seats needed to retake working control of the House.
